comment: brief TRN-7 R-trn7-2. micromamba's single static program, checksummed, installs conda-forge's ngspice into an environment of circuitRF's own: no conda installation of the user's is read or changed. conda-forge's newest ngspice is 41, and it builds none for arm64 (checked 2026-11-15 on its package index), so macOS arm64 and Linux arm64 have no recipe and say so instead. Run end to end in a Debian x64 container (2026-11-15).
layoutNote: A conda environment writes its own absolute path into the files it installs, so the home is built where it stays.

sources.checksumNote: micromamba 2.10.0 checks every package it downloads against the SHA-256 conda-forge's index lists for it; ngspice-exe is pinned to its exact build, 41 hb224a76_0

consentNotes: ngspice is free software under the modified BSD licence, with parts under other free licences listed in its own documentation; circuitRF starts it as a separate program and distributes nothing.
micromamba is free software under the BSD licence; circuitRF runs it only to install ngspice and deletes it afterwards.

steps.name: Install ngspice 41 from conda-forge
steps.comment: --no-rc and --override-channels: no .condarc of the user's, and no channel but conda-forge, plays any part.

steps.name: Clear micromamba's package cache
steps.comment: The cache holds every package a second time, and nothing reads it again. clean takes no --root-prefix: it reads MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX, which this recipe sets.

measured.source: circuitRF's own install in a Debian x64 container (emulated on an M4), 2026-11-15: 25 s and 0.17 GB after the package cache was cleared; ngspice 41 then ran the testdata/transient/ngspice benches
